question: Retake A Site Split 3v2, spike planted, 30s. You are Sage at A Heaven (overlooking the site), 1 ATK spotted below, 1 unknown. How do you run the retake?

options.label: Exploit the Heaven high-ground to clear the site from above with your team, Slow Orb on the spike to delay defuse
options.explication_courte: On Split, retakes are won through verticality: from Heaven you can see post-plant positions below, Slow Orb delays the defuse, and your team enters from the low angles simultaneously.

options.label: Drop down to the ground level and retake the site grouped with your team through the low entries
options.explication_courte: A grouped low-ground retake is solid, but you abandon the unique vertical advantage of Heaven - the ATK below have less information without the top-down threat.

sources_option.citation: High-ground positions like A Heaven define combat on Split; Split rewards owning a vertical position over winning a horizontal gunfight, so giving up Heaven cedes the edge.

options.label: Wall (Barrier Orb) the site entry and wait for the timer to force the ATK to move before retaking
options.explication_courte: Placing a passive wall in a 3v2 you favor loses the round: the spike is planted, YOU are the one who must defuse - letting the timer run is a slow forfeit.

sources_option.citation: In a spike-planted retake the defenders own the clock pressure; passively walling and waiting hands the round to attackers who only need to survive on the plant.

options.label: Solo peek from Heaven onto the spike without waiting for your team for a fast pick
options.explication_courte: A solo Heaven peek without a trade offers the ATK a free kill: if you die, the retake becomes a 2v2 without your Heaven advantage and you lose the numbers edge.

sources_option.citation: When retaking on Split, take space together and clear crossfires; peeking solo from Heaven without a trade donates a free duel and wastes your utility advantage.

explication_longue:
Situation: 3v2 retake on A Site Split, spike planted, 30 seconds. You are Sage at A Heaven - the high-ground that dominates the site - with Slow Orb, Barrier Orb, Healing Orb; 1 ATK spotted below, 1 unknown.

Split A retake is won through verticality: Heaven overlooks the post-plant positions, and a team that combines high-ground (Heaven angle) with low-ground (Ramp/Lobby entries) forces the 2 ATK into an impossible coverage problem. Sage's Slow Orb on the spike delays the defuse, buying the extra seconds needed to coordinate the entry.

The correct sequence: Slow Orb onto the spike (delay), your two teammates push through the low entries while you cover from Heaven - the 2 ATK cannot hold both simultaneously. Dropping to low ground (acceptable) is solid but wastes the Heaven advantage. Walling the entry and waiting (costly) is passive in a situation where you must defuse the spike - the timer is your enemy. Solo Heaven peek (mistake) throws the numbers advantage away.

Estimated elite distribution: ~55% Heaven high-ground + Slow Orb + coordinated low entry, ~22% grouped low-ground retake, ~15% passive wall wait (costly), ~6% solo Heaven peek (mistake).

sources.citation: High-ground positions define combat on Split: A Heaven, B Tower, Rafters and Mid Vents all offer sightline advantages; Split rewards owning a vertical position.
For A site, controlling Heaven and screens provides the best coverage; always check Heaven positions before clearing ground level, and pre-aim elevated spots on retake.
Save key abilities for post-plant, take space together, clear crossfires and isolate duels with utility; a coordinated retake beats a rushed one.

La position du 2e ATK est inconnue (design) ; s'il tient Heaven-access, l'avantage vertical de Sage se reduit — ce que trancherait un juge.
